meta.title: Finding Gold — The exploration funnel
meta.author: Ezekiel Minja
meta.description: Finding Gold: a field guide to mineral exploration. Educational — not a design standard.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Exploration is not searching. It is elimination, run cheapest first.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: One. Reconnaissance. Regional, cheap, across huge areas. Maps, satellite data, old reports, stream sediments. What comes out is a licence application and a shortlist of ground.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Two. Target generation. Walk the ground. Map it, sample the soil and the rock, fly geophysics. What comes out is a ranked list of anomalies.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Three. Target testing. Drill. This is the first genuinely expensive step, and most targets die here. What comes out is an intercept, or a reason to walk away.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Four. Resource definition. Drill the thing that worked, on a grid, until the grade and the shape are known well enough to model.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Five. Studies. Scoping, pre-feasibility, feasibility. Can it be mined, processed, permitted, financed and closed? What comes out is a reserve, and a decision.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Here is the part nobody tells students.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Of a thousand serious prospects, about a hundred get drilled. Around ten return something interesting. And roughly one becomes a mine. From the first look to the first gold is commonly seven to fifteen years.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: It is mostly failure. The craft is in failing cheaply.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Every stage exists to spend a little money ruling out a lot of ground, so the expensive tools only ever get pointed at the few places that have earned them.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Spend drilling money on a target that satellite data and a soil grid could have killed for a thousandth of the cost, and you have not been unlucky. You have been disorganised.
